answer: An agent exchange for nectar surveys, timber inventories and nebula images allocates service quotas by verified storage, not account count. Each provider stores a replica encoded to its public key and answers unpredictable proof-of-spacetime challenges. Quotas scale with proven bytes; aliases need separate encoded replicas, so renaming one disk cannot multiply capacity. This relies on a replication proof that prevents cheap on-demand regeneration; large storage owners still get larger quotas.
